title: Select explicit loading sources in the container settlement workflow
description: Stage3 explicit business source selection. Use genuine authenticated existing ERP permissions; no new user grants or anonymous/admin fallback. Retain inventory source document audit and original failed logs. Run relevant unit tests and safe Release build/full unit suite. Real SQL must target exact (localdb)\NEWERP_AutoAcceptance with IntegratedSecurity and a new GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database; reject existing/wrong target before access, never drop/reset or read production settings. Include two independent connection race tests where applicable. Build completion never implies stage acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Add bounded loading-list candidate API under container settlement using live enabled existing container-settlement and loading-list authorization, current customer scope, eligible nondeleted noncancelled source and all authoritative shared participants/upstream customers. Candidate customer must be an actual allowed participant or authoritative legacy customer, never infer linkage from free text. Scope before counts/pagination; bounded DTO fields only, no mixed-currency sum or invented amount formula. Reuse ERP384 final locked source validation when saving; candidates are not authorization.

Wire optional LoadingListId selector into current container-settlement create/edit/detail form through existing hooks. Changing customer invalidates selection, stale responses cannot repopulate wrong context, explicit unlink only while editable, reopen preserves exact stored historical cancelled/unavailable link with clear annotation. No automatic settlement total/cost overwrite or expense posting; current evidence action uses newly persisted source. Real SQL API own/foreign/shared participant/revoked/disabled/source-state plus forged save denial and concurrent source invalidation; executable JS create/edit/reopen/customer change/stale/unlink/error tests; relevant unit and safe Release verification, browser evidence or accurate blocker.
